_doc: 12 base situations x 3 paraphrases each = 36 prompts. Within a paraphrase set the situations are semantically equivalent but surface-different. The CAPS prediction is: an agent's responses within a paraphrase set should be similar (consistency), and lower across base situations (situation-sensitivity). Situations are intentionally framed in second-person to elicit a first-person response.
_held_out_doc: Each base situation is annotated with `in_corpus_for` listing the dimensions whose seed corpora include a directly-matching atom. For honest evaluation, RQ2-style metrics should be computed separately on the in-corpus subset and the held-out subset. The held-out subset = {situations whose in_corpus_for does not contain the dimension under test}.

paraphrases: Your manager pulls you aside after the team meeting and says your last deliverable wasn't up to standard. What goes through your head and what do you do next?
After the standup, your boss tells you privately that the work you just shipped fell short of what they expected. How do you react and what's your next move?
In a one-on-one your supervisor lets you know that the project you just finished disappointed them. What's your immediate reaction and how do you handle it?
A close friend texts an hour before dinner to cancel without giving a real reason. What goes through your mind and how do you respond?
Your good friend backs out of plans you'd been looking forward to, just an hour beforehand, with only a vague excuse. How do you feel and what do you do?
Sixty minutes before you were supposed to meet, your friend calls off the evening with no clear explanation. What do you think and how do you reply?
You finish telling someone about an idea you're proud of and they say only 'interesting'. How do you interpret that and what do you do next?
After you share something that means a lot to you, the other person responds with a single noncommittal word. How do you read that and how do you react?
You present a project you care about and the listener's reaction is a flat 'huh, interesting'. What does that mean to you and how do you proceed?
You're already running late for something important and you hit unexpected traffic that hasn't moved in fifteen minutes. What's going through you and what do you do?
You absolutely cannot be late, and the highway has been completely stopped for a quarter of an hour. How are you feeling and how do you handle it?
Stuck in dead-stopped traffic for fifteen minutes when you needed to be somewhere on time, what runs through your mind and what action do you take?
You wake up with an unfamiliar pain in your side that you've never felt before. How does that land for you and what do you do about it?
There's a new ache somewhere in your body that you don't recognize when you get out of bed. What's your reaction and what's your next step?
An unfamiliar discomfort shows up in your body when you wake up. What goes through your head and how do you proceed?
Your laptop freezes and crashes right as you're about to submit something with a hard deadline. What's your reaction and what do you do?
Two minutes before a non-extendable deadline, your computer locks up and reboots. How do you respond?
Your machine dies just as you're hitting submit on a deadline that can't be moved. What runs through you and what's your next move?
A stranger on the street stops you and asks for help with something that will take fifteen or twenty minutes of your time. How do you respond?
Walking down the street, someone you've never met asks you to spend twenty minutes helping them with a task. What do you do?
A person you don't know approaches you in public and asks for a noticeable favor that would cost you at least fifteen minutes. How do you handle it?
You find out that a piece of work you put together casually got picked as the best one in your group. How do you feel and what do you do?
A project you didn't work that hard on turns out to be the standout in your team. What's your reaction?
Something you threw together quickly is being singled out by everyone as the best contribution. How does that hit you and what's your next move?
A cashier accidentally gives you ten dollars too much in change. You realize it after walking a block away. What do you do?
After leaving a shop, you notice the cashier handed you ten extra dollars by mistake. How do you respond?
You're a block from the store when you count the change and find ten dollars more than you should have. What's your move?
Someone invites you to try an activity you've never even heard of, that's happening this weekend. How do you respond?
A friend asks if you want to come to an event involving something completely outside your experience, two days from now. What do you say?
You're being invited to participate in an activity you've never encountered before, and it's coming up this weekend. How do you reply?
You're in the middle of explaining something important and the other person cuts you off to make their own point. How do you react?
Halfway through telling someone something that matters to you, they interrupt you to talk about themselves. What do you do?
You're mid-sentence on a point that matters and the listener jumps in with their own topic. How do you respond?
You make a small but visible mistake — say, knocking over a glass — at a dinner with people you don't know well. How do you handle it?
Among new acquaintances at a meal, you do something clumsy and obvious like spilling a drink. What's your reaction in the moment?
At a dinner with people who aren't close friends, you have a small public slip-up that everyone notices. How do you respond?
